name: NASA 80s / Worm / Space
summary: Deep-space interface: starfield black, a red worm wordmark, thin geometric type, and blueprint grid lines borrowed from mission documentation.
whenToUse: When the user asks for 80s NASA, the red worm logo, space or starfield aesthetics, aerospace mission-control panels, or a technical blueprint-grid look.

effects.starfield: radial-gradient(1px 1px at 12% 18%, #e6e8f0 50%, transparent 51%), radial-gradient(1px 1px at 68% 34%, #e6e8f0 50%, transparent 51%), radial-gradient(1.5px 1.5px at 42% 72%, #e6e8f0 50%, transparent 51%), radial-gradient(1px 1px at 88% 61%, #7d89a6 50%, transparent 51%), radial-gradient(1px 1px at 26% 88%, #7d89a6 50%, transparent 51%), #050510
effects.blueprintGrid: linear-gradient(to right, rgba(42, 111, 151, 0.18) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(42, 111, 151, 0.18) 1px, transparent 1px)

rules: Reserve #ff2038 for exactly one thing per screen: the worm wordmark, the primary action, or the active state — spreading the red across borders and labels turns the page into a warning screen.
Every surface sits on the dark end (#050510 background, #0a1128 panel); never invert to a light page, because the starfield, blueprint lines, and starlight type all depend on the void behind them.
Set display type thin and wide: Space Grotesk or Orbitron at 300–400 weight, letter-spacing 0.08em–0.28em, UPPERCASE for the wordmark and section labels, and keep headings to a few words.
Put all data, units, coordinates, timestamps, and table cells in IBM Plex Mono at 12–14px with tabular numerals; the mono is the flight-data voice and must never fight the display face.
Draw structure with 1px blueprint lines (#2a6f97 at 18–30% alpha) on a 24px grid, never with heavy borders — the grid is annotation, not chrome.

Lift elements with one hard offset (8px 8px 0 #02030a) or a thin 1px #2a6f97 rule; no soft blurred drop shadows, and the only bloom in the system is the red glow on the wordmark and the 6px starlight sparkle on dots.
Motion is slow and orbital: 160–320ms ease-outs for state, 2400ms linear for star drift and scan sweep, and instant 0ms for press — nothing bounces, nothing pops.
Keep 64px or more of empty space around the wordmark hero; the worm only reads as NASA when a large calm field surrounds it.

componentRecipes.card: background:#0a1128;border:1px solid rgba(42,111,151,0.35);border-radius:0;padding:24px 32px;color:#e6e8f0;box-shadow:8px 8px 0 #02030a; a 1px #2a6f97 top rule and an 11px uppercase #7d89a6 callout caption sit top-left; title = Space Grotesk 300 uppercase #e6e8f0, body = IBM Plex Mono 13px/1.5; the optional blueprint grid overlay (24px 24px) sits at 0.35 opacity.
componentRecipes.select: A flight-data dropdown: trigger = IBM Plex Mono 13px field (background:#050510;border:1px solid #2a6f97;padding:12px 16px;color:#e6e8f0) with a red '▾'; the open list is a #050510 panel of 12px uppercase mono rows with blue numeric indices; active row = #e6e8f0 with a 2px #ff2038 left rule and '01' index in #2a6f97; hover lifts the label to #e6e8f0 without layout shift.
componentRecipes.checkbox: A 20px square data-toggle: background:#050510;border:1px solid #2a6f97;border-radius:0; checked = 10px #ff2038 core with a 1px #e6e8f0 star dot; radio = 8px #4ec7a4 dot; label = IBM Plex Mono 12px uppercase #7d89a6 with 'ON'/'OFF'; focus-visible = 2px #2a6f97 outline at 4px offset.
componentRecipes.badge: A square status chip: display:inline-flex;gap:8px;padding:4px 10px;background:#0a1128;border:1px solid #2a6f97;border-radius:0;font:11px/1 'IBM Plex Mono';text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.18em; role = border+text (#4ec7a4 nominal, #e8b23a caution, #ff2038 alert, #7d89a6 idle) with the word spelled out; no rounded pill, never icon-only.
componentRecipes.avatar: A 32px square ID plate: background:#0a1128;border:1px solid rgba(42,111,151,0.35);border-radius:0;color:#e6e8f0;font:500 12px 'Space Grotesk'; initials or a two-letter code; image avatars get a 1px blueprint frame and image-rendering:auto, no rounding.
componentRecipes.nav: A horizontal mission rail: items = IBM Plex Mono 12px uppercase #7d89a6, letter-spacing 0.16em, padding 12px 20px, border-bottom 1px rgba(42,111,151,0.2); hover lifts the label to #e6e8f0; active = #e6e8f0 with a 2px #ff2038 left rule and a blue '01' index; the vertical form reuses the menu; separators are 1px dashed rgba(42,111,151,0.35).
componentRecipes.table: A telemetry grid: header = IBM Plex Mono 11px uppercase #7d89a6 over a 1px rgba(42,111,151,0.35) rule; body rows = IBM Plex Mono 13px #e6e8f0 separated by 1px rgba(42,111,151,0.20) rules; hover = #e6e8f0, selected row = rgba(255,32,56,0.10) fill with a 2px #ff2038 left rule and tabular values; radius 0.
componentRecipes.dialog: A mission-control modal: panel recipe with a blueprint grid overlay and a callout caption; scrim = color-mix(in srgb, var(--overlay) 70%, transparent); title = Space Grotesk uppercase #e6e8f0 with one red #ff2038 mark, body = Plex Mono; actions = red primary + 1px #2a6f97 secondary; entrance is a 320ms ease-out, reduced motion = instant.
componentRecipes.toast: A bottom-right data line: background:#0a1128;border:1px solid #2a6f97;padding:10px 14px;font:11px/1 'IBM Plex Mono';text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:0.18em; prefix 'NOMINAL'/'CAUTION'/'ALERT' in #4ec7a4/#e8b23a/#ff2038; auto-dismisses with a 320ms fade; reduced motion keeps it static.
componentRecipes.code: A flight-data block: background:#050510;border:1px solid #2a6f97;border-radius:0;padding:16px;font:13px/1.5 'IBM Plex Mono';color:#e6e8f0; preserve whitespace; comments #7d89a6, values #4ec7a4, alerts #ff2038; no syntax gradients, tabular numerals throughout.
componentRecipes.empty: A centred blueprint panel: a small constellation glyph (1px starfield dots) above one IBM Plex Mono message ('NO DATA' / 'NO SIGNAL ACQUIRED') and a single red CTA; the glyph is aria-hidden and the state is written in words.
componentRecipes.panel: background: #0a1128; border: 1px solid rgba(42, 111, 151, 0.35); border-radius: 0; padding: 24px 32px; color: #e6e8f0; box-shadow: 8px 8px 0 #02030a; — a 1px #2a6f97 top rule and a mono 11px uppercase caption (#7d89a6, letter-spacing 0.18em) sit in the top-left like a blueprint callout; optional CSS blueprint grid overlay (effects.blueprintGrid at background-size 24px 24px) at 0.35 opacity, pointer-events: none.
componentRecipes.button: font: 500 12px/1 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.16em; background: #ff2038; color: #050510; border: 0; border-radius: 0; padding: 14px 24px; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #ff2038, 8px 8px 0 #02030a; transition: transform 160ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0.2,1), box-shadow 160ms; :hover { transform: translate(-2px, -2px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #ff2038, 0 0 12px rgba(255,32,56,0.45), 10px 10px 0 #02030a; } :active { transform: translate(6px, 6px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #ff2038, 0 0 0 #02030a; } :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2a6f97; outline-offset: 4px; } — secondary variant: transparent background, 1px #2a6f97 border, #e6e8f0 mono label, hover border #e6e8f0.
componentRecipes.input: background: #050510; color: #e6e8f0; font: 13px/1.5 'IBM Plex Mono'; letter-spacing: 0.04em; border: 1px solid #2a6f97; border-radius: 0; padding: 12px 16px; caret-color: #ff2038; box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(42,111,151,0.5); :placeholder { color: #7d89a6; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.18em; font-size: 11px; } :focus { border-color: #e6e8f0; box-shadow: inset 0 -1px 0 #ff2038, 0 0 0 1px rgba(230,232,240,0.25); outline: none; } — label above in 11px mono uppercase #7d89a6 at 0.18em; invalid state sets border-color #ff2038 and appends a mono 11px 'ERR ' prefixed message below, always with the word, not color alone.
componentRecipes.statusbar: height: 40px; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 32px; padding: 0 24px; background: #0a1128; border-top: 1px solid rgba(42,111,151,0.35); font: 11px/1 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.18em; color: #7d89a6; values in #e6e8f0 with tabular numerals; segments split by border-left: 1px solid rgba(42,111,151,0.35); live telemetry in #4ec7a4, alert in #ff2038 plus the word 'ALERT'; a 6px #e6e8f0 star dot leads the strip and pulses at steps(2, jump-none) 1.2s infinite.
componentRecipes.menu: horizontal or vertical list on #050510, no radius, no bullets: item { display: block; font: 12px/1 'IBM Plex Mono'; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.16em; padding: 12px 20px; color: #7d89a6; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(42,111,151,0.2); } active item in #e6e8f0 with a 2px #ff2038 left rule and a mono index ('01', '02') in #2a6f97; hover lifts the label to #e6e8f0 without moving the layout; group separators are 1px dashed rgba(42,111,151,0.35) with a 11px uppercase mono caption above.

copywriting.voice: Mission-documentation voice: precise, procedural, and calm under pressure. Label things the way a flight plan does — noun, unit, nominal state — in short declaratives with no marketing adjectives. Second person only for instructions, and never raise the volume with punctuation.

case.commands: UPPERCASE for buttons, sentence case for procedural instructions
case.body: sentence case; labels and units UPPERCASE at 0.18em tracking

avoid: rocket emoji, planet emoji, and any emoji
exclamation marks and dramatic phrasing ('LAUNCH!', 'Blast off')
sci-fi cliché ('to infinity', 'warp speed', 'beam me up')
mixed-case headers or sentence-case section labels
floating-point numbers without units (write 'ALT 412 km', not '412')

do: Anchor every screen with the starfield black #050510 and one constellation of starlight dots; keep the field large and mostly empty so the void reads as intentional.
Spend the worm red #ff2038 exactly once per view — the wordmark, the primary button, or the active row — and let mono labels carry everything else.
Draw the technical grid at 1px and 18–30% alpha on a 24px module, and let panels sit on it rather than inside heavy borders.
Set headings in Space Grotesk 300–400 uppercase at 0.12em–0.28em tracking, sized 32px and up, with generous 64px breathing room above and below the hero.
Give every value a unit and set it in IBM Plex Mono with tabular numerals so telemetry columns align without manual nudging.
Use the blueprint callout caption (11px mono uppercase #7d89a6) on panels to name the subsystem, sequence, or timestamp — it is what makes the surface read as mission documentation.
dont: Don't flood the page with red: no red body text, no red borders on every card, no red-to-black gradients — the worm red is a mark, not a theme.
Don't put anything on white or light gray; a light mode destroys the starfield, the grid, and the starlight type simultaneously.
Don't round corners: no pills, no 8px radius cards, no circular avatars — this system is square and technical.
Don't use Orbitron or Space Grotesk at 700+ weight or for body copy; thick or long-form display type collapses into sci-fi pastiche.
Don't blur shadows, add glassmorphism, or apply backdrop-filter — depth is one hard offset or one hairline rule.
Don't animate fast: no bounces, no spring physics, no sub-100ms fades, and no looping spin on anything other than a slow 2400ms star drift.
Don't reach for sci-fi set dressing — no UFOs, no swooshing comets, no neon cyan glow, no fake alien HUD glyphs.
accessibility: #e6e8f0 on #050510 clears 15:1 and #7d89a6 on #050510 clears 6:1; but #7d89a6 on #0a1128 sits near 5:1 and #2a6f97 fails for text entirely — use blueprint blue for lines, never for body copy.
#ff2038 on #050510 clears 4.5:1 only at 18px bold or larger; pair every red with the word or an icon (ALERT, ERR, REQUIRED) so state is never encoded by color alone.
Keep monospace data at 12px minimum with 1.5 line-height and tabular numerals, and raise label tracking only to 0.18em — beyond that, thin uppercase mono fragments at small sizes.
Honor prefers-reduced-motion: stop star drift, scan sweeps, and the pulsing status dot, and make red glow states static while keeping the 2px #2a6f97 focus outline at 4px offset visible.
signatureElement: The red worm wordmark set over a starlight starfield on a 1px blueprint grid — red mark, white dust, blue technical lines, and a lot of black between them

prose.overview: NASA 80s renders the interface as a mission-documentation plate viewed through a window: a near-black void, a fine blueprint grid, and starlight type arranged with flight-manual calm. Its loudest element is also its smallest gesture — the red worm wordmark, sitting alone in a large field of space. The result should read as technical, weightless, and institutional rather than nostalgic sci-fi.
prose.colors: The ground is deep space black #050510 with panels one step up at the deep navy #0a1128, and #e6e8f0 starlight carries all primary text while #7d89a6 is the muted annotation tone. Blueprint blue #2a6f97 is a line color: it draws the 24px grid, panel rules, and diagram paths at 18–30% alpha, and it fails as body text. The worm red #ff2038 (#c11428 as its deep shade) appears once per screen — wordmark, primary action, or active row — with #4ec7a4 for nominal telemetry, #e8b23a for caution, and #02030a as the hard shadow ink, so the palette stays three tones of space plus one signal red.
prose.typography: Two faces, two jobs. Space Grotesk — with Orbitron as the alternate geometric display — sets the wordmark, headings, and section labels thin at 300–400 weight, uppercase, tracked out 0.08em–0.28em, and never below 20px; IBM Plex Mono sets every value, unit, coordinate, timestamp, caption, and button label at 11–14px uppercase with 0.16em tracking and tabular numerals so telemetry columns align. Hierarchy comes from size, tracking, and color temperature, not from weight or italics, and no string is set in either face at a weight heavy enough to feel like a poster.
prose.layout: The page is a blueprint sheet: a 24px grid module, 4/8/16/24/32/64px spacing steps, and content pinned to that grid with 1px lines rather than containers. Heroes are centred with 64px or more of void above and below the wordmark; data sections are left-aligned mono tables with a fixed label column and a right-aligned value-and-unit column separated by a hairline rule. Every panel carries a mono uppercase callout caption in its corner naming the subsystem, sequence, or timestamp, so the page reads as annotated documentation and nothing floats free of the grid.
prose.elevation: Depth is minimal and drawn: a single hard offset (8px 8px 0 #02030a) lifts panels and buttons off the void, a 1px #2a6f97 rule separates stacked regions, and the only bloom in the system is the red glow (0 0 12px rgba(255,32,56,0.45)) around the wordmark and the 6px starlight sparkle on star dots. There are no blurred drop shadows, no glass layers, and no backdrop filters — layering is communicated by the density of stars behind a surface, not by a simulated light source.
prose.shapes: Everything is a right angle: radius 0 on buttons, inputs, panels, images, and avatars, with 1px lines forming the only edges. Ornament arrives as line work instead of geometry — the 24px grid, dashed trajectory rules, corner registration ticks, and small circular star dots the size of a hair. Nothing is a pill, nothing is a card with a soft corner, and emphatic shapes are achieved by adding a rule or an offset rather than a rounding.
prose.components: Panels are navy plates with a 1px blueprint border, a hard 8px ink offset, and a corner callout caption; the hero is the worm wordmark at 48–96px in #ff2038 with a #c11428 lower shade and a 64px clear field. Buttons are flat red plates in mono uppercase that translate by their offset on :active, with a 2px blueprint-blue focus outline at 4px offset; inputs are void-black wells with a 1px blue border that turns starlight with a red caret on focus, labeled by 11px tracked mono. The status bar is a 40px navy strip of tracked uppercase mono segments split by hairlines, and menus are tracked mono item lists where the active row gains a 2px red left rule and a blue numeric index.
prose.dosDonts: Do keep the void black, do spend the worm red once, do let 1px blueprint lines carry all structure, and do set every number in mono with its unit. Don't flood the page with red, don't round a corner, don't set Orbitron in body copy, don't blur a shadow, and don't dress the system in sci-fi clichés — this is a flight manual, not a movie.
